{{Short description|French mathematician}}
'''Sébastien Boucksom''' (born 26 August 1976 in [[Roubaix]]) is a French mathematician.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sébastien Boucksom|website=CNRS|url=http://sebastien.boucksom.perso.math.cnrs.fr/}}</ref>

Boucksom studied at the [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]] from 1996 to 1999, when he qualified with his [[agrégation]] in mathematics. He received his doctorate in 2002 from the Institut Fourier of the [[Université Grenoble Alpes]] with thesis ''Cônes positifs des variétés complexes compactes'' under the supervision of [[Jean-Pierre Demailly]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id = 64161}}</ref> As a postdoc Boucksom studied with [[Simon Donaldson]] at [[Imperial College London]]. From 2003 he did research for the [[CNRS]] at the Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu of the CNRS and the [[University of Paris]] VI. Since 2010 he has been a part-time professor at the [[École Polytechnique]] and since 2014 a [[Academic rank#France|directeur de recherche]] of the CNRS at the Center de Mathématiques [[Laurent Schwartz]] of the École Polytechnique.<ref>{{cite web|title=CV, Sébastien Boucksom|website=CNRS|url=http://sebastien.boucksom.perso.math.cnrs.fr/CV/CV.pdf}}</ref>

Boucksom's research deals with [[algebraic geometry]], geometry of [[p-adic number|''p''-adic]] [[Algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]], and [[Kähler manifold]]s. Ideas introduced by Boucksom and collaborators [[Robert J. Berman|Berman]] and Jonsson using non-Archimedean geometry to study Kähler manifolds have been very influential in the study of [[K-stability of Fano varieties]].<ref>Robert Berman, Sébastien Boucksom, Mattias Jonsson. A variational approach to the Yau–Tian–Donaldson conjecture. To appear in the Journal of the AMS</ref>

In 2014, the [[French Academy of Sciences]] awarded him the [[Prix Paul Doistau–Émile Blutet]]. The laudation cited his work on positive fluxes in compact [[Kähler manifold]]s with application to characterization of pseudo-effective cones,<ref>Boucksom, Paun, Demailly, Peternell, The pseudo-effective cone of a compact Kähler manifold and types of negative Kodaira dimension, J. Algebr. Geom., Vol. 22, 2013, pp. 201-248, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405285 Arxiv 2004]</ref> as well as his work on the [[Monge-Ampère equation]] with application to the existence of [[Kähler-Einstein metric]]s with minimal singularities.<ref>S. Boucksom, P. Eyssidieux, V. Guedj, A. Zeriahi, Monge-Ampère's Equations in Big Cohomology Classes, Acta Mathematica, Vol. 205, 2010, pp. 199-262, [https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3674 Arxiv]</ref> With [[Robert J. Berman|Berman]] and Nyström, he proved a version of the [[Fekete problem]] in pluripotential theory.<ref>Robert Berman, Sebastien Boucksom, David Witt Nyström, Fekete points and convergence towards equilibrium measures on complex manifolds, Acta Mathematica, vol. 207, 2011, pp. 1-27, [https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2820 Arxiv]</ref> (An algorithmic version of the Fekete problem is problem number 7 of [[Smale's problems]].)

In 2018, Boucksom was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Variational and non-Archimedean aspects of the Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Boucksom, Sébastien|title=Variational and non-Archimedean aspects of the Yau--Tian--Donaldson conjecture|year=2018|eprint=1805.03289|class=math.DG}}</ref>
